She snaps a twig off the marked tree. 'The pre-written hand wasn't the king's. I know that now. I didn't then. I just knew a survey that arrives before the surveyor is a lie with paperwork, and I don't sign lies. So I quit. And I never found out what happened to my green groves.'

choices.label: Pre-written findings, the Astrologer's hand. Tell her what she brushed against.
choices.resultText: She listens, very still. 'He was WRITING my forests before he'd read them.' The twig snaps again in her fingers. 'I quit over bad paperwork and it was the end of the world wearing a survey stamp. I want to see what he did with my groves.'

choices.label: Ask what happened to the foresters who signed
choices.resultText: 'Promoted,' she says flatly. 'Every one. Good postings, crown pensions.' A pause. 'Verram signed forty of them. His letters stopped making sense two winters later. Kept using phrases that weren't his. I thought it was drink.' She looks at the marker. 'It wasn't drink.'

title: What She Saw (Your Report, Filed)
body:
At the first crown marker, Yara pulls a folded page from her jacket before you can say a word.

'Found this in my kit this morning. My handwriting. YOUR report (the Astrologer, the pre-written surveys, Verram's letters), all of it, written down like I'd heard it before.' She hands it over: it is, word for word, the briefing you gave her in a rendering that no longer happened.

'So I've done my grieving over the paperwork already, somewhere the sky misfiled.' She re-pockets the page and unslings her bow. 'Good. Saves daylight. Take me to my groves.'

choices.label: Take her to the groves
choices.resultText: Prepared lands better than surprised: she walks her old survey lines dry-eyed and deadly accurate, cataloguing exactly what the pre-written hand did to green ground. The file grows. The file is a weapon now.

title: The Stand She Didn't Take
body:
A day off the route, exactly where her memory said: the grove she was marched away from. What the quarantine order did to it afterward is written in stumps and nine years of scrub. But at the heart, defiant, stands a copse of old oaks the loggers never reached. Green. Still green.

Yara walks in among them and puts her hand on the biggest, and stands there a long time.

'I looked the other way once,' she says finally. 'Whole career, one time, under orders, and it was HERE.' She turns, and her face is a forester's official notice. 'I'd like to take the stand now. Nine years late. Mark this grove guild-warded. I'll cut the blazes myself. Anyone who logs it answers to the guild, and the guild answers to me.'

choices.label: Ward the grove: her blazes, the guild's word
choices.resultText: She cuts the warding marks with a steady hand. HER survey, ground-truthed, signed by walking every foot of it. The stand she didn't take, taken. Nine years is a long time to carry an unspent refusal; she leaves it in the bark where it belongs.

choices.label: Ward it, and name it the Ellswood Stand in the guild's records
choices.resultText: 'You don't name groves for living foresters,' she objects, cutting blazes the entire time she objects. The name goes in the ledger. She never mentions it again. She visits every expedition that passes within a half-day.

title: A Warden's Oath
body:
Yara pins a page to the muster board: good paper, careful hand, three words.

*WE LOOK. ALWAYS.*

'Forester's oath, guild edition,' she says. 'The crown's oath was four pages of loyalty and one clause about the land. Backwards. So: three words, no clauses.' She taps the page. 'Every scout, every warden, every survey this guild ever runs: we look. At blight, at markers, at pre-written lies, at whatever's actually THERE. Nobody in this guild ever gets ordered to look the other way. Put it in the charter and I'll believe in charters again.'

choices.label: Into the charter: three words, no clauses
choices.resultText: It goes in exactly as written. Recruits think it's simple until their first corrupted survey line, and then they understand it's the whole job. Yara checks the muster board every morning, the way other people check the weather.

choices.label: Adopt it, and give her the wardens to hold it
choices.resultText: Warden-captain Ellswood, first of the office. Her survey standards are merciless, her ground-truth absolute, and no finding in guild records is ever again written before the walking. The Astrologer pre-writes many things. Not her forests. Not anymore.

title: The Oath, Re-Pinned
body:
Yara stands at the muster board holding a page she just wrote, staring at four pin-holes in the cork that exactly fit its corners.

'Three words,' she says. 'WE LOOK. ALWAYS. I wrote them fresh this morning and the board's already worn where they hang.' She pins the page into its own ghost. 'The groves, the blazes, the oath. I've taken this stand before, somewhere the sky misfiled. Taking it again is just ground-truthing.' She turns. 'Confirm the survey. All of it.'

choices.label: Confirm the survey
choices.resultText: Groves warded, blazes cut, oath re-pinned into its remembered holes: nine years of unspent refusal, spent twice now, and holding. Some stands, once taken, stay taken across any weather the sky can write.

title: The Granary Road
body:
The road is ordinary now: cart ruts, weeds, a marker stone. Odile walks it counting under her breath.

'Forty-one wagons,' she says. 'This road, that night. I held the gate behind us for six hours so the granaries could empty: grain first, then people, then the garrison, then me.' She stops at the marker stone and rests her hand on it like a shoulder. 'Everyone remembers the province fell. I remember it fell EMPTY. The Astrologer's people took walls and a treasury. The wagons took everything that was actually mine to lose.'

She looks down the road, the direction the wagons went. 'A marshal without a province. The books don't say what that is.'

choices.label: It's a marshal whose province is on wagons. Still hers.
choices.resultText: She's silent a long moment. 'Forty-one wagons of province,' she says at last, testing it. 'Scattered across two kingdoms.' Her shoulders square by a degree that changes her whole silhouette. 'Then I'm not retired. I'm DEPLOYED. I should do a muster.'

choices.label: Ask about the sixth hour at the gate
choices.resultText: 'The sixth hour was the one past sense,' she says simply. 'Hours one through five were the plan. Hour six was because the last wagons were slow and the plan wasn't the point.' She taps the marker stone. 'Banners burn. Wagons roll. Choose what you defend accordingly.'

title: The Scattered
body:
The resettlement is eleven families in a village that had room for eight: her province's people, three years on, with new roofs and old accents. The first one to spot her drops a water bucket.

By the time Odile reaches the green, the whole cluster has turned out, and someone says it, the title she hasn't heard since the gate: 'MARSHAL.'

What follows is not a reunion; it's a MUSTER, and she can't help it and neither can they. Names, health, roofs, stores, griefs, all reported in and received with a commander's full attention. At the end an old man asks the question they've clearly kept warm for three years: 'Marshal. Where do we plant the banner, when there's a banner again?'

choices.label: Let her answer
choices.resultText: She's quiet a long moment. Then: 'The banner burned. What I kept is standing in front of me reporting in.' She looks around the green. 'When there's a banner again, it plants wherever you are. That was always the rule. The province was never the walls.' The muster ends with dry eyes on no one.

choices.label: Tell them where the Marshal serves now
choices.resultText: The old man hears 'the guild that argues with the sky' and nods slowly. 'Then we know where to send the young ones who want to matter.' Over the next year, they do. Three of the guild's steadiest recruits carry her province's accent.

title: The Scattered (Found Twice)
body:
The resettlement turns out before Odile is halfway up the road, not surprised, EXPECTING her, the way a garrison expects an inspection it was warned about.

The old man meets her at the green. 'Marshal. You found us again.' He says AGAIN with a countryman's certainty about things he can't explain. 'Second time you've walked up that road. First time, the sky took back. We kept the feeling anyway. Roofs remember being counted.'

Odile looks down the muster line already forming, in a rendering where she never held this muster, and her parade face nearly fails her.

choices.label: Hold the muster the roofs remember
choices.resultText: Names, roofs, stores, griefs, all reported to a marshal they've now trusted across two versions of the world. The sky can redeal provinces. It has apparently never once managed to redeal loyalty. She notes it for the campaign's files: strategic asset, unmakable.

title: Colors
body:
Odile stands at the gatehouse at dawn with a wrapped bundle and the bearing of a woman at a flag ceremony only she can see.

'The pole's been empty since I arrived,' she says. 'Empty banner pole over a defended gate. It's been shouting at me for a lunation.'

She unwraps the bundle: a banner, new-sewn, her needlework, with guild colors in the field and in the canton, small and precise, a single grain-sheaf on a wagon wheel. 'Your colors. My freight.' She looks up the pole. 'I held one gate six hours for what was behind it. This gate holds back the end of the world. Marshal requests permission to raise colors, and to hold this one for the duration.'

choices.label: Permission granted: raise the colors
choices.resultText: The banner takes the dawn wind like it was commissioned for it. Odile watches from parade rest, and when she finally turns away she's someone with colors again, which, for a marshal, is the whole difference between retired and READY.

choices.label: Granted, and give her the gate watch entire
choices.resultText: Gate-Marshal Vantrec, standing orders her own. The watch rotas acquire a precision that alarms and then delights Dagny and Miro both. The pole is never empty again. She's already sewn the replacement, 'because you always sew the replacement.'

title: Colors, Re-Raised
body:
Odile meets you at the gatehouse with a finished banner in her hands and a quartermaster's frown.

'I sewed this in four evenings without a pattern,' she says. 'Guild colors, grain-sheaf on the wheel. Except my hands knew the measurements. This banner has flown from THAT pole, and I have never raised it.' She snaps the fabric taut. 'The road, the muster, the colors: I've served this whole posting before, somewhere the sky retreated from. Marshal requests permission to resume the duration.'

choices.label: Resume the duration
choices.resultText: Road walked, muster held, colors raised: a full tour of duty re-completed in days, on muscle memory and roofs that remember being counted. The pole takes the banner like a gate takes its marshal: as a matter of long standing.

title: Marginalia
body:
Petra leads you into the frozen library wing with a catalogue of her own haunting: forty-one appearances of her handwriting in books she never touched, indexed by shelf, ink, and 'apparent mood.'

'Entries one through forty are corrections,' she says. 'Copyist's notes. Sums checked, dates fixed. Me being useful in books I've never opened. Unsettling but PROFESSIONAL.'

She stops at a held-open ledger, ten thousand books hanging mid-flight around you. 'Entry forty-one is different.' Her finger hovers over the margin. In her unmistakable hand, beside nothing in particular, it says: *Petra, when you find this, you are not losing your mind. You are keeping it in more than one place.*

choices.label: She's been leaving herself messages across renderings. Tell her what the sky does.
choices.resultText: She listens to the whole truth (the re-readings, the unmakings, the loom) pale and electric at once. 'So somewhere in the shuffle, a me who KNEW wrote to a me who wouldn't.' She touches the margin. 'That's not haunting. That's GOOD ARCHIVING.'

choices.label: Ask what entry forty-one is next to
choices.resultText: Nothing. That's the thing. Blank page, deliberate placement: a note that could only be FOR her, not about anything. 'She wanted my attention, not my corrections,' Petra says slowly. 'Past me understood filing. You put the important thing where nothing else competes.'

title: Marginalia (Entry Forty-Two)
body:
Petra meets you at the library wing already holding the catalogue, and it's thicker.

'Entry forty-two is new,' she says, walking you to the held-open ledger. Below the old note, in her hand, dated a year this world never had: *Petra, the one who brought you here has done it before. Trust the continuity. Skip the panic; it wastes a lunation. Love, us.*

She looks up. 'It says LOVE, US. I sign notes to MYSELF as a collective now.' A beat. 'I'm going to need the whole truth again, apparently, but the short version, since my archive says you keep it somewhere.'

choices.label: Give her the short version: the panic-skipping edition
choices.resultText: The loom, the renderings, the correspondence, all delivered in the efficient form her own note requested. She catches up in an afternoon instead of a lunation, then writes entry forty-three: *Confirmed. The short version works. Us.*

title: The Note She Leaves
body:
Petra has set up in the scriptorium with her best ink, three drafts, and stage fright.

'If some next Petra reads what this Petra writes,' she says, 'then this is the most important copying job of my life, and I keep FRIVOLOUSLY drafting.' She shows you draft three: instructions, reassurances, an index to her catalogue, a joke. 'There has to be a joke, she'll be frightened, I'M frightened and I'm the one writing...'

She squares the page. 'Witness it. Not because it needs a witness. Because SHE needs to know I didn't write it alone, that there was someone in the room who knew about both of us and stayed anyway.'

choices.label: Witness the note, and add one line in your own hand
choices.resultText: You write it at the bottom: *She's telling the truth. I'll be here too. Find me.* Petra reads it, blinks hard, and copies the note fair with both signatures. 'Now it's a DOCUMENT,' she says thickly. 'Two witnesses. Unimpeachable.'

choices.label: Suggest where to file it: beside entry forty-one
choices.resultText: 'Where nothing else competes,' she agrees. The note goes into the held ledger's margin-shadow, addressed to a woman who doesn't exist yet, from a woman who won't remember writing it, witnessed by the one person who'll remember both.

title: Correspondence
body:
Petra finds you at a dead run, catalogue clutched to her chest, entirely incoherent for the first ten seconds.

'There's a REPLY.' She drags you to the ledger. Beneath her witnessed note, beneath YOUR line, new ink, her hand, but aged into the page like it's been there years: *Received. All well here, or as well as an unmade year can be. The joke landed. Tell the witness the continuity holds both ways. P.*

'It's not from the next one,' she whispers. 'It's from a PREVIOUS one. From a year the sky already took. The correspondence goes BACKWARDS too.' She sits down on a library step, catalogue in her lap, awed and small. 'I'm not haunted. I'm not even an archive. I'm a POST OFFICE.'

choices.label: A post office needs a postmistress. Make it official.
choices.resultText: Petra Quillane, Keeper of the Correspondence: a desk in the frozen wing, custody of the margins, standing orders to log every letter the renderings pass through her hands. The loom finally has a clerk. The clerk, for the first time in her life, feels entirely un-borrowed.

choices.label: Ask what she'll write back
choices.resultText: She thinks a long time, then writes one line and shows no one, files it in the margin-shadow, and closes the catalogue. 'Between us,' she says, meaning all of them, every Petra the sky ever drafted. Some correspondence doesn't need a witness. It needs a family.

title: The Post Office, Reopened
body:
Petra meets you in the library wing, where a desk you never saw installed stands in the margin-shadow of the held ledger, and on it, waiting, a note in her hand: *Re-opening checklist. You know the drill by now. Us.*

'There's a CHECKLIST,' she says, torn between outrage and delight. 'I left myself onboarding materials. Catalogue, note, witness line, desk: the whole correspondence, pre-filed.' She sits down at the desk that was always going to be hers. 'Witness the re-opening. It's on the checklist. Item four. You're item four.'

choices.label: Be item four
choices.resultText: Witnessed, checked, reopened: the post office of the renderings back in service in a single afternoon. She stamps the checklist DONE and files it where the next reopening will find it. The continuity, as promised, holds both ways.

title: Thirty Years of Not Knowing
body:
The sanctum is a ring of standing stones around a door that no longer holds anything, and Harl walks its perimeter once, fully, before he'll go near the center: thirty years of patrol in a single lap.

'Post at dawn, walk the ring, check the seals, post at dusk,' he says. 'Ten thousand days, give or take. Never knew what was behind it. Wasn't ALLOWED to know. The not-knowing was the job. A warden who knows starts making judgments about what's worth what.'

He reaches the door, open now, empty now, and puts his hand flat on it, the first time in thirty years he's touched it.

'Then it opened from the OUTSIDE, and the seal I felt break was the whole spine of my life going slack at once. So here's my question, and take your time: was it worth guarding? Because I can bear the answer. I just can't bear not asking anymore.'

choices.label: Tell him the truth: a Seal Fragment, a piece of the world's own binding
choices.resultText: He takes it standing, like weather. 'A piece of the sky's own lock.' Slowly, thirty years re-sort themselves behind his eyes. 'Then every day mattered. Every dawn lap.' He pats the empty door once, gently. 'Good. GOOD. I could have guarded a wine cellar and never known.'

choices.label: Ask first what he HOPED it was
choices.resultText: 'Something patient,' he says at once. 'Thirty years I told myself: whatever needs guarding this hard is either terrible or precious, and either way it's PATIENT. It waits, I walk.' He half-smiles. 'A fragment of the world's seal. Patient as stone. I guessed closer than I feared.'

title: Seeing It
body:
Harl asks formally, hat literally in hand, to see the fragment his life guarded. Standing up, he specifies. A warden views his charge standing up.

Brought before it, he does not touch it, does not speak, does not move for four full minutes. Thirty years of dawns and dusks passing between a man and the thing he kept without knowing.

'Smaller than I dreamed it,' he says at last, hoarse. 'Bigger than everything.' He straightens into what can only be called attention. 'I have one request and I've practiced it: I don't want it BACK. It's yours now; you opened the door fair. I want to know it's kept WELL. Show me its post. Show me the seals. Warden's professional courtesy. Then I can stand down properly, and not one dawn before.'

choices.label: Walk him the full inspection: post, seals, watch rota
choices.resultText: He inspects like a man auditing his own soul's bookkeeping, and at the end gives the nod of one warden to another's work. 'Kept well,' he pronounces. 'Better post than mine. More honest, anyway. Your guards get to KNOW.' He stands down that evening, thirty years, zero regrets, one lap of the campus wall out of pure habit.

choices.label: Let him stand one watch over it: a proper last shift
choices.resultText: Dusk to dawn, his post, one final time: voluntary, ceremonial, absolute. In the morning he reports the watch uneventful in a voice that closes a thirty-year book. 'Relieved at dawn,' he says, and means every layer of it.

title: Seeing It (The Watch Already Stood)
body:
Brought before the fragment, Harl stops mid-stride, then laughs, one dry note, the sound of a man catching the universe in clerical error.

'I've stood here.' He points at the floor by the door. 'THAT spot. Dusk to dawn. My knees remember the stones: a last watch I never stood, relieved at a dawn that never came up.' He looks at the fragment a long moment, and the four minutes of silence become one.

'The sky redealt my whole life's question,' he says, 'and kept my ANSWER. Fine. Warden's courtesy, the short form: show me the seals are sound, and I'll stand down the way I apparently already did.'

choices.label: Show him the seals: the short form
choices.resultText: Inspection passed, watch acknowledged across renderings, warden stood down twice and finally. 'Most men don't get to retire once,' he notes, hanging up an authority no one ever gave him and no one could take. 'Thorough life, this one.'

title: A Door Worth a Warden
body:
Harl presents his findings the way he does everything: methodically, standing, hat under arm.

'I have inspected every door in this campus. All of them.' He produces a list, and you don't doubt it's exhaustive. 'Storerooms, cellars, the records hall, the long gallery. Sound doors, most. Good hinges. But there is exactly one door in this place, in this WORLD, that holds what my old post held. The kind of kept thing that keeps everything else.'

He means the campus itself: the anchor, the held Second, the one door the Astrologer cannot open.

'Thirty years I guarded a sealed thing without knowing. I'm asking for the other job now. Let me guard a kept thing KNOWING. Days at the records hall, nights on the ring wall. A warden's no good without a door, and begging your pardon...' the ghost of a smile, '...this is the best door I've ever seen.'

choices.label: Give him the door: Warden of the Anchorhold
choices.resultText: He takes up the post the same hour: dawn lap, seal check, dusk lap, ten thousand days of practice brought to the one door that deserves them. The campus gains a fixture. Wren charts his rounds for her thesis. He pretends not to be pleased.

choices.label: Give him the records hall too: keeper of kept things
choices.resultText: Fragments' provenance, the Hall's ledgers, the vault seals, all under one methodical eye. Between Harl's doors, Sable's web, Dagny's Round, and Odile's gate, the campus becomes, quietly, the best-warded ground in any rendering of the world.

title: The Post, Resumed
body:
Harl finds you at dawn, mid-lap. HIS lap, the campus ring, walked at patrol pace with seal-checks at intervals nobody ever showed him.

'Caught myself doing it three mornings running,' he says, falling in step. 'Dawn lap. This route. These checkpoints. A post I never held, worn into my boots.' He stops at the gatehouse and stands to attention out of thirty years' habit. 'The sanctum, the viewing, the door. I've served this post before, somewhere the sky relieved me of it. Reinstate the warden. The door's been waiting and so, apparently, have I.'

choices.label: Reinstate the warden
choices.resultText: Post resumed mid-lap, seals checked, thirty-plus-one years of service reconciled in a morning. The best door he's ever seen gets its warden back, and the dawn lap becomes, again, as reliable as the dawn.

title: The Collection
body:
Tamsin holds the campfire like a stage, three stories in, each one polished to a killing edge: the bridge that wasn't there, the duel fought in a flooded church, the winter she guarded a man who turned out to be two children in a long coat.

Then, gauging the fire's warmth just so, she brings out the manuscript. Oilskin-wrapped, thick, corners soft with travel.

'The saga,' she says. 'Working title: *The Guild That Argued With the Sky.* Everything you people do goes in here: the shards, the audiences, the campus that shouldn't exist. I've collected stories my whole life. This is the first one big enough to spend a life ON.' She pats it. 'I take commissions on chapter titles. I do not take edits.'

choices.label: Ask to hear the guild's chapter so far
choices.resultText: She reads twenty minutes by firelight, and it's GOOD: your own campaigns, rendered mythic and true at once, everyone recognizable and slightly taller. When she stops, nobody speaks for a moment. 'That's the reaction I keep the pen for,' she says, satisfied.

choices.label: Ask which of her three stories was true
choices.resultText: 'All of them,' she says, wounded. Then, honest: 'The FACTS wander. The stories are true. That's the trade. I'm not a chronicler, I'm a KEEPER. Petra files what happened. I keep what it MEANT.' The distinction, you realize, is a creed.

title: The Chapter She Skips
body:
You've heard Tamsin tell forty stories, and mapped the hole in the middle of them: every saga has a hedge-knight, and the hedge-knight has no hedge, no house, no before.

When you finally ask, she's quiet long enough that you think she'll deal a deflection off the bottom of the deck. Instead she pokes the fire and tells it plain, no polish, the first unpolished thing you've ever heard from her.

'House Greywood was six farms and a name. Debt took it. No fire, no villains, just arithmetic and a bad decade. They struck our name off the rolls while I was off collecting stories worth more than mine.' She looks up. 'I skip the chapter because I can't FIX it in the telling. Everything else I keep, I keep well. That one I just... have.'

choices.label: Some chapters aren't kept. They're carried. Say so.
choices.resultText: She turns the words over like a coin. 'Carried, not kept.' A slow nod. 'That's the sentence I've been circling for nine years. It goes in the saga: chapter unnumbered, one page, carried.' She writes it that night. It stays one page. It stays IN.

choices.label: Point out the guild's rolls have room for a name
choices.resultText: 'Greywood, on a roll again.' She laughs, then stops, because it's not nothing. It goes in the muster book that week, her hand steadier than usual. 'Six farms and a name,' she says. 'The farms are gone. Turns out the name travels.'

title: The Shelf That Keeps
body:
Tamsin stands at the edge of the frozen library wing, manuscript under her arm, negotiating with visible awe.

'Ten thousand books hang in this room, and the unmake can't touch one of them.' She turns. 'My whole trade has one enemy: forgetting. Fires, floods, heirs who can't read. And this room is the one shelf in creation the sky can't clear.'

She holds up the saga. 'Terms: the manuscript lives HERE, in the held light, updated every time I'm home. In exchange, the guild gets its saga kept where endings can't reach it.' A breath, and there it is, under the showmanship, the actual stake: 'Everything I've ever kept got lost eventually. Everyone. I'd like to keep ONE thing somewhere the arithmetic can't find it. And then, personally, I intend to outlive my material, but that's chapter last, and I don't spoil endings.'

choices.label: Grant the shelf: the saga enters the Second
choices.resultText: You walk her through the edge; she places the manuscript on an empty shelf between hanging books, where it will be mid-kept forever. She stands looking at it a long moment. 'Un-forgettable,' she says finally, meaning it literally, meaning it entirely.

choices.label: Grant it, and commission the saga as the guild's official chronicle
choices.resultText: Keeper of the Guild's Story, by appointment: commissions on chapter titles, no edits, updates every homecoming. She shakes on it and immediately retitles three chapters out of pure celebration. The record of the guild that argues with the sky now argues alongside it.

title: The Shelf That Keeps (Her Book Is Already On It)
body:
At the library wing's edge, Tamsin stops mid-negotiation, staring past you into the held light.

On a shelf between hanging books, where no book of hers has ever been placed, sits a manuscript. Oilskin-wrapped. Corners soft with travel. HERS. The saga, complete through chapters she hasn't written yet, in a rendering that no longer happened.

She walks in and reads standing up for an hour. When she comes out her eyes are wet and her grin is enormous. 'The ending's not spoiled,' she reports. 'She skipped chapter last too, and left a note instead: *finish it yourself, coward. T.G.*' She hefts her own working copy. 'I have NOTES from MYSELF. This is the best material I have ever been handed.'

choices.label: Shelve the new draft beside the old
choices.resultText: Two sagas, side by side in the held light: the story and its retelling, arguing companionably across renderings. She updates both, forever after, and lets exactly one person per year read the note. It keeps morale astonishing.

title: Chapter Last, Deferred Again
body:
Tamsin meets you with the manuscript packed and the negotiation pre-concluded.

'Shelf in the frozen wing, updates every homecoming, no edits, name on the muster rolls, one carried chapter.' She ticks them off on her fingers. 'I've struck this deal. The terms are worn smooth in my mouth like a story on its fortieth telling. The sky redealt the world and kept my CONTRACT, which honestly is the most flattering review of my negotiating I have ever received.' She shoulders the saga. 'Re-execute the terms. The shelf's waiting. It remembers the weight.'

choices.label: Re-execute the terms
choices.resultText: Shelf granted, saga placed, name entered, chapter carried: the whole deal re-struck in an afternoon. Chapter last remains unwritten, on schedule, by a keeper who fully intends to keep outliving her material, one rendering at a time.
